content: Individuals who are not equipped with the appropriate protective clothing and equipment must not enter the leak or spill area until the cleanup process is fully completed. 3. All potential sources of ignition must be removed from the vicinity of the leak or spill to prevent fire or explosion hazards. 4. The area where the leak or spill has occurred must be adequately ventilated to prevent the accumulation of harmful vapors. 5. Any spilled EGBE (ethylene glycol butyl ether) or EGBEA (ethylene glycol butyl ether acetate) must be contained and absorbed using materials such as vermiculite, sand, or paper towels. 6. Small amounts of absorbed material should be placed under a fume hood, allowing sufficient time for the liquid to evaporate and for vapors to clear the ductwork. 7. 8. Contaminated absorbent materials must be disposed of as hazardous waste in compliance with applicable regulations. 9. The spill area must be thoroughly cleaned with water to remove any residual contamination. 10. Only personnel who are trained in emergency procedures and adequately protected against the hazards of glycol ethers should be involved in spill cleanup, leak control, and repair activities. 11. 12. 13. Safety showers, eyewash stations, and washroom facilities must be readily available, maintained in working condition, and accessible to workers in areas where skin or eye contact with EGBE or EGBEA is likely. 14. If EGBE or EGBEA is splashed or spilled on a worker, contaminated clothing must be removed immediately, and the affected skin must be thoroughly washed with soap and water. 15. If EGBE or EGBEA comes into contact with the eyes, they must be irrigated immediately with a copious flow of water for at least 15 minutes. If irritation persists, the worker should seek medical attention. 16. EGBE and EGBEA must be stored in cool, well-ventilated areas and kept away from acids, bases, and oxidizing agents to prevent hazardous reactions. 17. 18. In areas where EGBE or EGBEA is produced or used, the storage, preparation, dispensing, or consumption of food and beverages, as well as the storage or application of cosmetics and tobacco products, must be strictly prohibited. 19. Employers must provide handwashing facilities and encourage workers to use them before eating, smoking, using the restroom, or leaving the worksite. 20. Protective clothing, equipment, and tools must be cleaned periodically to maintain hygiene and safety. 21. Employers must arrange for the cleaning, laundering, or disposal of contaminated work clothing and equipment. Any person responsible for cleaning or laundering these items must be informed that they may be contaminated with EGBE or EGBEA, which can cause adverse hematologic (blood) and central nervous system effects. 22. The work area must be cleaned at the end of each shift (or more frequently if necessary) using vacuum pickup methods. Collected wastes must be placed in sealed containers with labels indicating their contents. 23. Cleanup and disposal activities must be conducted in a manner that prevents worker contact with wastes and complies with all applicable local, state, and federal regulations. 24. 25. 26. Employers must also maintain accurate medical records for each worker subject to medical monitoring, including the physician's written statement, results of medical examinations and tests, medical complaints, and any other pertinent information. 27. 28. 29. Employers must comply with regulations regarding the transfer of records as outlined in applicable federal standards. 30. 31. 32. 33. The recommended standards are intended to protect workers from the acute and chronic effects of EGBE and EGBEA and to guide management and labor in developing better engineering controls and healthier work practices. 34. Extrapolation beyond the occupational environment may not be warranted. 35.
